title: The no-shard test does not depend on thread finish order
why: hooks/test_mutate_shared.py ShardTests.test_no_shard_runs_all asserts ran == ["a","b","c"], but mutate_shared.run_mutants runs entries on a ThreadPoolExecutor, so ran fills in finish order. Under a loaded lane-lint run it failed twice for lane mail-read-receipt (#3137, 10:26 CST Nov 13) with ["a","c","b"]. Alone it passes (6 of 6 on main). It is a flaky test, not red on main. Sighting 00:26 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 00:26, relayed): hooks/test_mutate_shared.py:119 test_no_shard_runs_all failed lane lint on #3343 (["a","c","b"] != ["a","b","c"]; mutants run in parallel, the recorded order is not fixed). The lane reruns once and sends run ids. Step mutate-shard-test-order-flake is folded into this step and stays folded. Second report 00:35 CST Nov 14 (lane local-allow-goes-global, relayed; the coordinator asked it): merge --lane-lint on PR 3343 head 3f401217cf at 00:17 CST failed job "Mutation verdict fixture suite" at hooks/test_mutate_shared.py line 119 (["a","c","b"] != ["a","b","c"]); the test passes alone in 15 s; the lane's diff does not touch mutate_shared; a rerun on the same head is running and the lane will say "flaked once" with both run ids if green. The lane called it a possible regression of step mutate-shard-test-order-flake: that step is folded into this one, whose fix (lane shard-order-test-flake, PR unread) is not on main, so this reads as the same open flake, unchecked. Third report 00:42 CST Nov 14 (lane local-allow-goes-global, relayed): the same failure repeated on a rerun of PR 3343 head 3f401217cf at 00:40 CST, so it failed 2 of 2 in lane lint, not once. The lane read the cause from the code: the test's fake run_one appends to a list from pool worker threads in mutate_shared.run_mutants, so with more than one worker the recorded order races. The lane read step mutate-shard-test-order-flake as done; it is folded into this step, whose fix (compare sorted(ran), lane shard-order-test-flake) is not on main as far as triage has read. Sighting 05:00 CST Nov 14 (consultant 04:59, via the coordinator 05:00; neither read the failing run): ShardTests.test_no_shard_runs_all still races on thread order (a,c,b against a,b,c) after #3149 merged at 23:01 CST Nov 13. NOT reopened: the fix landed in bedbce7b5c80 and an earlier "still failing" case (PR #3343) turned out to be a branch that predated the fix. Reopen when a failing run id is read and its head contains bedbce7b5c80; then red first under load. Asked: the run id and the branch head. Reopen request 05:01 CST Nov 14 (consultant 05:00): a local lane lint on #3349 head 3128df369 failed at 04:55 CST on ShardTests.test_no_shard_runs_all (got a,c,b, expected a,b,c) while a second lint ran on the same machine. NOT reopened: triage read the file at both refs (GitHub contents read). At #3349's head 3128df369c the test is still the old order-sensitive form, `self.assertEqual(self.run_shard(None, list("abc"))[1], list("abc"))`. On main 48728d122be0 it is the fixed form: it runs with finish_in_reverse False and True and compares `sorted(ran)`. So #3349 carries the old test (the same pattern as #3343): the failure is the old test, not a gap in the fix. The consultant's "#3149 did not cover this case" does not follow from it. The remedy is to merge main into #3349 (the coordinator/runner 10's act), not to reopen. Reopen only if the fixed form fails. Confirmed 05:07 CST Nov 14 (runner 10 05:06, relayed): its first lane lint on #3349 failed on the old order-sensitive test (the head predated bedbce7b5c80) and the rerun alone passed; #3349 merged 05:03. Same finding as triage's file reads above: no reopen.
